skill.name: functionality-audit
skill.description: Validates code behavior through sandbox testing, execution checks, systematic debugging, and clear reporting. It helps users confirm that generated or modified code works with realistic inputs before release.
skill.summary: Verifies that code works by running focused tests and debugging failures in isolated environments.
skill.author: DNYoussef

content.value_statement: Generated code can appear correct while still failing under real inputs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through sandbox testing, debugging, and evidence-based reporting.
actual_capabilities: Creates isolated test environments that avoid production side effects.
Designs test cases for normal flows, boundaries, errors, and edge cases.
Executes code with realistic inputs and verifies expected outputs.
Analyzes failures through reproduction, tracing, and root cause investigation.
Documents test results, identified bugs, remediation progress, and follow-up recommendations.
limitations: Requires clear expected behavior to judge whether outputs are correct.
May need project-specific dependencies, test data, or services before execution.
Cannot guarantee production behavior when important systems are mocked.
Complex cloud or container environments may require extra setup time.

use_cases.title: Validate Generated Code
use_cases.description: Run focused tests after AI code generation to prove the implementation works with representative inputs.

use_cases.title: Debug Unclear Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce failures, inspect execution paths, and identify root causes before applying fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Checks
use_cases.description: Perform final execution verification and document risks before shipping a change.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after a small code change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the functionality-audit skill on these files. Confirm the code runs, test the main expected behavior, and report any failures with reproduction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Test Edge Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this implementation with normal inputs, boundary values, malformed inputs, and empty inputs. Compare actual behavior against the expected behavior I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Failing Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Systematic investigation of a known bug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use functionality-audit to reproduce this failure, identify the first incorrect behavior, explain the root cause, and propose a minimal fix with regression tests.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Release Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full functionality audit for this release candidate. Create an isolated environment, run realistic tests, summarize pass and fail results, rank discovered bugs, and list remaining release risks.

output_examples.input: Audit a new data parser before merging it.
output_examples.output: The report lists tested input types, expected outcomes, actual outcomes, three passing cases, one malformed-input failure, and a recommended validation fix.
The audit reproduces the failure under concurrent requests, identifies a race in state updates, and recommends a focused regression test.

output_examples.input: Check a release candidate for deployment readiness.
output_examples.output: The summary states the pass rate, critical defects, unresolved risks, and targeted follow-up tests needed before release.

best_practices: Provide expected behavior, representative inputs, and known edge cases before the audit starts.
Run tests in an isolated environment that mirrors important production assumptions.
Use audit results to add regression tests for every confirmed bug.
anti_patterns: Assuming code works because it compiles or passes lint checks.
Changing code before reproducing the failure and understanding the root cause.
Testing only the easiest happy path while ignoring errors and boundaries.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: It can recommend or help verify fixes, but its main purpose is testing, debugging, and reporting.

faq.question: Can it use existing test suites?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run existing tests and add focused cases when current coverage is incomplete.

faq.question: Does it require a sandbox?
faq.answer: A sandbox is strongly preferred because it reduces risk from side effects during execution.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide file paths, expected behavior, test data, dependencies, and any known failure symptoms.

faq.question: Can it audit cloud integrations?
faq.answer: Yes, when safe emulators, mocks, or non-production cloud resources are available.

faq.question: How is this different from static analysis?
faq.answer: Static analysis inspects code structure. This skill runs code and compares actual behavior with expected behavior.
